title: The first step of an axis
hook: Connect a hormonal signal with a target.

knows: Hormones can carry signals through the blood to target tissues.
doesNotKnow: Thyrotropin-releasing hormone from the hypothalamus stimulates TSH release from the anterior pituitary.

misconception: All hormones come from one gland and act on every cell.
objective: Identify the stated endocrine signal and its target in a simplified pathway.

claims.text: Question, diagram and explanation: Which hypothalamic releasing hormone stimulates the anterior pituitary to release TSH? Thyrotropin-releasing hormone from the hypothalamus stimulates TSH release from the anterior pituitary.
The diagram shows one selected source–target pathway, not all hormone effects or feedback loops.
Recall: In the stated example, which source releases TRH into the circulation? Thyrotropin-releasing hormone from the hypothalamus stimulates TSH release from the anterior pituitary.

recall.question: In the stated example, which source releases TRH into the circulation?
recall.why: Thyrotropin-releasing hormone from the hypothalamus stimulates TSH release from the anterior pituitary.
